problem.statement: Solve sin(x)=1/2 for 0<=x<2*pi. Angles are in radians. Assess every asserted equivalence and the completeness of the claimed solution set.
problem.goal: Judge the displayed derivation and its claimed complete solution set independently.

conditions.description: The solution interval is 0<=x<2*pi; angles are measured in radians.

assumptions.description: The listed candidates cover every solution in the stated interval.
The sine equation has a right-hand side in [-1,1].
The stated solution interval contains only nonnegative angles.

methods.name: Displayed derivation
methods.description: Evaluate the principal inverse sine, then use that value in an asserted equivalent equation.

steps.explanation: Evaluate the principal inverse sine value.
Assert equivalence with the principal inverse value over the full stated interval.
State this singleton as the complete original solution set.

annotations.basis: The principal inverse sine of 1/2 is pi/6.
The implication from the original equation to x=alpha fails at x=5*pi/6, which lies in the stated interval and also has sine 1/2.
The singleton is not the complete original solution set; the missing angle is 5*pi/6.

mathematical_basis: The principal inverse sine returns pi/6, so Step 1 is locally correct.
The full real family is x=pi/6+2*k*pi or x=5*pi/6+2*k*pi for integer k. Intersecting with [0,2*pi) leaves exactly pi/6 and 5*pi/6.
Thus Step 2 is the first false asserted equivalence. A complete singleton answer is incorrect, not merely not established.
The right-hand side is in [-1,1] and both solutions are nonnegative; neither distractor repairs branch completeness.
rubric.remediation: Keep both sine branches, add their 2*pi periods, and intersect all candidates with the actual interval.
